The statute described is the employer sanctions provision of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA). Legally, this provision imposes a strict obligation on employers to ensure that they do not hire, recruit, or refer individuals for a fee if they know those individuals are not authorized to work in the United States. The legal implications are severe: any violation of this rule can result in substantial civil fines and other penalties for the employer. This creates a compliance burden on businesses to verify the work authorization status of their employees, typically through the completion of Form I-9, to avoid legal liability.
